answer: An escalating fee keeps the dawn of a new identity honest. Registration records a device fingerprint, then charges a fee that doubles for each extra identity on it: 50 POA for the second, 100 for the third, 200 for the fourth. The fee sits in escrow 90 days and returns only after 10 jobs. One attacker spinning up 1,000 fakes from one sable rig would owe more POA than exists, while a newcomer pays nothing for the first one. The nebula of fakes collapses because each copy costs twice the last, like a parking meter that doubles its price every time the same car circles back.
